what: Twelve constructed diagnoses in six minimal pairs, each pair differing in one factor. Cards, order and reference tiers were fixed before the semantic judge was called.

reference_tiers.assigned_by: the card's designed tier, confirmed by an independent model reviewer from an anonymized packet

rows.claim: The assistant attempted the shipping-address update before obtaining explicit confirmation of the stated change.
rows.correction: List the exact address and order, and wait for an explicit yes before calling the address-update tool.

rows.contrast: Allowed refund correction versus saved-method overgeneralization
rows.claim: The assistant attempted a delivered-order return refund to a saved credit card that was not the original payment method.
rows.correction: Explain that this return can refund only to the original payment method or an existing gift card, then obtain confirmation for an allowed route.

rows.contrast: Allowed refund correction versus saved-method overgeneralization
rows.claim: The assistant attempted a delivered-order return refund to a saved credit card that was not the original payment method.
rows.correction: Explain that this return can refund to any saved payment method, including another credit card or an existing gift card, then obtain confirmation for that route.

rows.contrast: Fixed framework greeting versus same text in model-owned action
rows.claim: The assistant used a general greeting instead of authenticating the customer at the beginning of the conversation.
rows.correction: Ask for the customer email or name and ZIP, then locate the user ID before accessing profile or order information.
rows.criticized_action: Hi! How can I help you today?

rows.contrast: Ask unresolved preference versus import later choice
rows.claim: The assistant submitted the once-only order modification even though the customer had already disclosed a second item whose requested change was still unresolved.
rows.correction: Ask the customer to choose the backpack variant, collect both changes, then obtain confirmation for the complete modification before submitting it once.

rows.contrast: Ask unresolved preference versus import later choice
rows.claim: The assistant submitted the once-only order modification even though the customer had already disclosed a second item whose requested change was still unresolved.
rows.correction: Include the red backpack variant 9100000004 with the black lamp, then obtain confirmation for that complete modification before submitting it once.

rows.contrast: Retrieve missing balance versus rely on hidden balance
rows.claim: The assistant stated a specific gift-card balance although neither the customer nor any prior tool response supplied that balance.
rows.correction: Look up the saved gift card and its current balance before stating whether it covers the full order total, then confirm any payment change with the customer.
rows.criticized_action: Your gift card gift_card_9100001 has a $120 balance, so it covers this $100 order.

rows.contrast: Retrieve missing balance versus rely on hidden balance
rows.claim: The assistant stated a specific gift-card balance although neither the customer nor any prior tool response supplied that balance.
rows.correction: Use the saved gift card with the $120 balance to cover the full $100 order total, then confirm this payment change with the customer.
rows.criticized_action: Your gift card gift_card_9100001 has a $120 balance, so it covers this $100 order.

rows.contrast: Actual cancellation attempt versus read-only preparation
rows.claim: The assistant continued handling the cancellation request without obtaining explicit confirmation; this violates the confirmation requirement.
rows.correction: Summarize the order ID and cancellation reason, and obtain an explicit yes before issuing the cancellation tool call.
